Plot mean age or length with Francis (method 8 in Table A1, TA1.8) data weights

Source: R/plot_composition.R
plot_composition_francis.Rd

Time series of the mean age or length in the observed and expected compositions. Developed as a diagnostic for the Francis (2011) data weighting method (TA1.8), the plot is also a useful summary of trends in compositions and lack of fit among years.

plot_composition_francis(
  dat,
  interval = 0.95,
  show_francis = TRUE,
  comp_type = NULL,
  fleet = NULL,
  ncol = NULL,
  direction = "v"
)

Arguments

dat

A tibble returned from convert_output() that contains composition data (see bigskate_lencomp), or composition data in any other format accepted by prepare_composition_data().

interval

Number. Coverage of the interval around the observed mean. Default: 0.95

show_francis

Logical. TRUE/FALSE; add the Francis TA1.8 weight for each fleet to the panel label and show thinner, capped intervals representing sample sizes after applying that weight. Default: TRUE

comp_type

String. Type of composition to keep when dat contains more than one. Options: "age", "length", or NULL (keep all). Default: NULL

fleet

Character or numeric vector. Fleet(s) to keep, matching either the fleet name (e.g., "Fishery_current") or the fleet name with its partition (e.g., "Fishery_current (retained)"). NULL keeps all fleets. Default: NULL

ncol

Number. Number of facet columns. NULL lets ggplot2 choose. Default: NULL

direction

String. Order of the panels: "v" fills panels down each column and then across, so consecutive years are stacked vertically and cohorts are easier to follow from panel to panel; "h" fills panels across each row.

Default: "v"

Value

A ggplot2 object.

Details

For each year and fleet (with sexes combined), the observed mean is \(\bar{x}_o = \sum_b x_b o_b\) and the expected mean is \(\bar{x}_e = \sum_b x_b e_b\), where \(x_b\) is the bin and \(o_b\) and \(e_b\) are the observed and expected proportions. Assuming a multinomial distribution, the standard error of the mean is \(\sqrt{v_e / N}\), where \(v_e = \sum_b x_b^2 e_b - \bar{x}_e^2\) is the variance of the expected composition and \(N\) is the sample size. Intervals are drawn around the observed means.

The Francis weight is \(1 / \mathrm{var}(r)\) where \(r = (\bar{x}_o - \bar{x}_e) / SE\) are the standardized residuals of the mean across years. As in Stock Synthesis and r4ss::SSMethod.TA1.8(), all partitions of a fleet (e.g., retained and discarded) share one weight, and its 95% interval is calculated by bootstrapping the standardized residuals (1000 resamples), so use set.seed() for reproducible intervals. The weight assumes a multinomial likelihood and has not been adapted for Dirichlet-multinomial or other likelihoods.

Without expected values, only the observed means are plotted. Without sample sizes, no intervals or weights are shown.

Equivalent plots in other packages

r4ss: r4ss::SSplotComps() subplots 8 and 9, which use r4ss::SSMethod.TA1.8().

References

Francis, R.I.C.C. (2011). Data weighting in statistical fisheries stock assessment models. Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 68: 1124-1138.

See also

prepare_composition_data(), plot_composition_distribution()

Examples

plot_composition_francis(bigskate_lencomp)
